sketches.title: Hold Music
sketches.premise: You are building one customer-service call, one step at a time. Start with a normal complaint; then make the next reply, transfer, promise, or mistake worse without losing track of what has already happened.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it is the next believable step in the same call and preserves every stated fact; a skipped link jumps past a needed response, an ending resolves or hangs up the call, and an undo reverses a stated step, while the score comes from how badly the move inconveniences, exposes, or humiliates the other player.
sketches.move_shape: Add exactly one spoken line or call event that directly follows the last one; for example, after “I was charged twice,” add “The agent says the second charge is for emotional support.”
sketches.first_card: A delivery app charged you for food that never arrived.

sketches.title: Ticket Escalation
sketches.premise: Together, build one support ticket from complaint to disaster. Each move adds exactly one status change, note, or handoff, and the ticket must still be the same case; the fun is making the other player look more useless while the case crawls upward.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it is one connected next record in the ticket, names no new case, and fits all earlier records; a skipped link changes status without its required action, an ending closes or cancels the ticket, and an undo restores an earlier status, while points reward blame, needless delay, or a note that makes the partner own the mess.
sketches.move_shape: Add one ticket entry after the current entry; for example, after “Assigned to Billing,” add “Billing marks it solved because the customer used the word ‘please.’”
sketches.first_card: A streaming service billed you after you canceled.

sketches.title: Supervisor, Please
sketches.premise: You are trapped in one customer-service call. Take turns adding the next escalation: a reply, a transfer, a policy, or a supervisor, until the call either gets fixed or becomes impossible to defend.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it follows directly from the whole call and keeps the same customer, problem, and phone line; a skipped link invents a jump with no connecting response, an ending gives a final fix or hang-up, and an undo takes back a spoken fact, while points reward the move that makes the partner wait, admit fault, or sound like a tiny tyrant.
sketches.move_shape: Add one next exchange or phone event; for example, after “The agent says the refund takes five days,” add “You ask why, and the agent says the five days are for finding the money.”
sketches.first_card: Your internet has been down since yesterday.

sketches.title: Policy Voice
sketches.premise: Build one customer-service call where every move adds a single new rule, excuse, or exception to the same complaint. The rules must stack cleanly; your job is to make the other player quote a policy so absurd that even the phone seems embarrassed.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds one rule or explanation that answers the current call without contradicting any earlier rule; a skipped link leaps to a later policy, an ending accepts or rejects the final answer, and an undo removes a stated rule, while points reward the most petty, personal, or costly rule aimed at the other player.
sketches.move_shape: Add exactly one new policy sentence that responds to the last one; for example, after “Refunds require proof,” add “Proof must be printed, but printers are not covered by our proof policy.”
sketches.first_card: You were charged a late fee even though the bill was paid early.

sketches.title: Transfer Chain
sketches.premise: Create one customer-service call by passing the same problem from desk to desk. Each move adds exactly one transfer or the first sentence after it, and every new desk must know why it received the call; make the other player inherit the worst part.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it names the next connected desk or reply and carries forward the entire problem and known history; a skipped link sends the call somewhere without a transfer, an ending hangs up or reaches a final answer, and an undo sends the call back to a prior desk, while points reward a transfer that wastes time, exposes incompetence, or leaves the partner responsible.
sketches.move_shape: Add one transfer or one opening line from the new desk; for example, after “Billing transfers you to Shipping,” add “Shipping says, ‘Great, what did Billing break?’”
sketches.first_card: A store sent you the wrong item and charged you for express shipping.

sketches.title: Case Notes
sketches.premise: Together, write the notes for one customer-service call as it goes bad. Each move adds one exact note from the same case, and the notes must form a clean record; the best play makes the partner’s future self look guilty, cheap, or spectacularly bad at reading.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it is one new chronological note that fits the full record and does not add a separate incident; a skipped link records an event with no place in the timeline, an ending marks resolution or abandonment, and an undo changes or erases an earlier note, while points reward a precise note that shifts blame, creates a trap, or makes the partner’s conduct impossible to explain.
sketches.move_shape: Add one dated or ordered case note after the last note; for example, after “Customer requests a manager,” add “Agent places customer on hold and orders lunch.”
sketches.first_card: A repair company says your covered repair is not covered.
